doc.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

chapter: Early life and path into trad jazz
title: Listening before playing, and high school and college trad groups
summary: He listened far more than he played, traded tapes with older collectors, and formed trad groups in high school and college without a music degree.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: That’s very interesting. Going from Basie, your interest in Basie, to playing in the small group traditional jazz, did you hear a lot of traditional jazz before you tried to play it?

Well yeah. I mean I heard the records that my parents had and then I started collecting as a teenager myself. So yeah I was listening a whole lot more in those days than playing. It took me ‘til really after college, as I say, before I learned to improvise very well.
Did you have any friends who shared your listening habits?
No, not my age. I traded with some older guys, tapes in the mail and stuff.
Oh I see. Your classmates were not into Turk Murphy.

Actually I did have a little traditional jazz group in high school. And I formed one in college and joined another one in college so back then there was a little bit of interest. But that was really going against the grain.
And then did you go on to get a music education degree?
Your interest in both education and performance is self directed?
